_comment: One specification for the derived column hints, asserted by BOTH implementations:
These are hand-written expectations, not generated output, so a change on either side fails on that
side rather than silently becoming the new truth. A user must see the same schema in Android Studio
as in VS Code; a divergence here is the bug class this file exists to prevent.
Each vector builds `CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, <column> <dbType>)`, inserts one row per
entry in `rows`, introspects, and compares the column's comment to `expect` (null = no comment).

Key NAMES are gated behind the host's cell-value opt-in, so these default-path vectors state the count. A stable map (per-user scores) has perfect recurrence and is structurally identical to a record, so no threshold separates them; see jsonHint in packages/core/src/column-hints.ts.
Identifiers in a hint are quoted the way the probe quotes them: unquoted, a mixed-case name folds and the suggested expression fails with "column ... does not exist".

vectors.name: a record whose keys recur is named
vectors.expect: JSON object, read with json_extract("prefs", '$.key') (2 recurring keys)

vectors.name: keys that never recur are usernames, not fields
a single recurring key is a one-tenant map, not a record
two repeat keys among many one-off ones are still a map
a key that is not identifier-shaped rejects the column outright
under three rows there is no evidence of reuse
only top-level keys are named
vectors.expect: JSON object, read with json_extract("doc", '$.key') (3 recurring keys)

vectors.name: an escaped quote inside a value does not end the string
vectors.expect: JSON object, read with json_extract("doc", '$.key') (2 recurring keys)

vectors.name: an object with no keys still gets the accessor
ordinary text is not JSON
malformed JSON is not JSON
a JSON array is described by its element type, not by keys
vectors.expect: JSON array of numbers; test membership with EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM json_each("ids") WHERE value = 1)

vectors.name: a column that is JSON in only some rows is not described
an integer timestamp in milliseconds states its unit
an integer timestamp in seconds states its unit
an id named like a moment is not a timestamp
a document number named like a moment is not a timestamp
an integer that is not a moment is left alone
a magnitude too small to be a modern timestamp says nothing
a unicode-escaped key is not a field name
an escaped delimiter inside a key is not a field name
escapes inside a value do not disturb the keys
vectors.expect: JSON object, read with json_extract("doc", '$.key') (2 recurring keys)

vectors.name: a JSON array of numbers names its element type
vectors.expect: JSON array of numbers; test membership with EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM json_each("ids") WHERE value = 1)

vectors.name: a JSON array of strings names its element type
vectors.expect: JSON array of strings; test membership with EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM json_each("tags") WHERE value = 'a')

vectors.name: an array of mixed types is not described
an array of objects is not a simple membership test
relaxed JSON5 with unquoted keys is not a JSON object
a Java Map.toString is not a JSON object
single-quoted keys are not JSON
content after the object means the text is not one object
two objects concatenated are not one object
prose wrapped in braces is not a JSON object
a comma inside a string does not split the array
vectors.expect: JSON array of strings; test membership with EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM json_each("names") WHERE value = 'a')

vectors.name: a brace inside a string does not make the array nested
vectors.expect: JSON array of strings; test membership with EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM json_each("tags") WHERE value = 'a')

vectors.name: leading zeros are not JSON numbers
Infinity is not a JSON number
a numeric literal with a suffix is not JSON
a key repeated inside one document counts once
vectors.expect: JSON object, read with json_extract("cfg", '$.key') (2 recurring keys)

vectors.name: a never-expires sentinel does not decide the unit
a column mixing seconds and milliseconds gets no unit
